simple.meaning: כָּלֶה (kâleh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “pining.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Deuteronomy, beginning at Deuteronomy 28:32. The surrounding contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּלֶה (H3616) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: כָּלֶה (kâleh) / H3616 is traced through Deuteronomy 28:32 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3616. kaleh [ כָּלֶה ] adjective failing with desire, longing , only feminine plural אֲלֵיהֶם וְכָלוֺת ראֹוֺת וְעֵינֶיךָ Deut 28:32 while thine eyes look and fail longingly for them (compare verb כלה Qal 2 b , and כִּלָּיוֺן below)

occurrences.englishText: Your sons and your daughters will be given to another people. Your eyes will look, and fail with longing for them all day long. There will be no power in your hand.
